_meta.title: Official ServiceNow source catalog
_meta.verified: 2026-11-04 — HTTP status checked from this environment (see status_2026_11_04)
_meta.rule: A topic is not learned until it has been read on an official ServiceNow source and confirmed on an instance. Blogs, videos and third-party courses are allowed only AFTER that, and are never the citation of record.
_meta.tos: Read manually, summarise in your own words, cite the URL. Do NOT bulk-scrape, crawl, mirror, or republish ServiceNow content. This repo deliberately contains zero scraped pages: the only automated fetching is a 7-request HTTP status check on the base URLs below.

ladder.name: Product documentation
ladder.use_for: Configuration steps, architecture, release notes, field and table definitions, plugin names, guided-setup step lists.
ladder.canonical_note: Docs are versioned per release: /docs/bundle/<release>-<product>/page/... The release segment changes every family release — prefer the docs search URL over a hardcoded deep path.

ladder.name: Now Create (Success Packs)
ladder.use_for: Success Packs: process guides, starter stories, implementation insights, architecture blueprints and recommended sequencing (Crawl → Walk → Run → Fly). The closest thing to an official 'how to implement this app correctly' package.
ladder.access: reached via Now Learning / ServiceNow University (search "Now Create"); nowcreate.servicenow.com itself wants a partner/customer login and returned no response from this sandbox on 2026-11-04
ladder.status_2026_11_04: learning.servicenow.com 200; nowcreate.servicenow.com 000 (blocked/timeout — known-good URL, unverified here)
ladder.note: If you only do one thing beyond the docs, do this: the Success Pack sequence is the difference between a working deployment and a rebuild.

ladder.name: ServiceNow University / Now Learning
ladder.use_for: Official courses, learning paths, free on-demand content, certification paths (CSA → CAD → CIS-ITSM/FSM/...), simulation labs.
ladder.access: free account; some content requires a partner/customer login

ladder.name: Developer portal + Personal Developer Instance (PDI)
ladder.use_for: The free instance you practise on, API Explorer (try REST calls live), official sample code, developer learning plans.
ladder.why_it_matters: Every lab in this repo assumes a PDI. No PDI, no proof — reading is not learning.

ladder.name: ServiceNow Community
ladder.use_for: Real-world gotchas, 'what we wish we knew', employee and partner posts, screenshots when docs are silent.
ladder.note: Peer content. Never authoritative — confirm on your instance before you teach it.

ladder.name: ServiceNow Store
ladder.use_for: App documentation and activation notes, which plugin/entitlement a capability needs, certified apps and spokes.

ladder.name: Now Support / Knowledge Base
ladder.use_for: Official KBs, troubleshooting, known errors, patch/release advisories.

allowed: Reading public documentation, Community posts, free Now Learning content and Developer site material
Writing your own beginner-friendly summaries, outlines and setup guides for personal or internal use
Reasonable copies of documentation for internal business use tied to your authorised ServiceNow use
Citing URLs with your own paraphrase
not_allowed: Automated scraping, spiders or bulk crawling of ServiceNow sites
Republishing large chunks of copyrighted material verbatim
Selling guides that are mostly copied ServiceNow content
how_this_repo_complies: No crawler or scraper ships here. scripts/sn_probe.js reads YOUR instance via your own login.
The only network calls are a 7-request HTTP status check in `sn_learn.py sources --check`.
Every doc paraphrases and links out; nothing is a doc mirror.

per_module_docs_search.note: Deep bundle paths embed the release name, so link the docs SEARCH query for a module rather than a fixed page. Replace spaces with +.

study_order: 1. Docs page for the module — skim the structure only (5 min); write down the 3 table names you saw
2. Now Learning course for that module, if one exists — 1.5x speed, no notes, just timestamps of 'aha' moments
3. PDI probe: run scripts/sn_probe.js, render the sheet (this repo) — now you know what YOUR instance actually has
4. Lab: do the hands-on thing, break it on purpose, fix it
5. Now Create Success Pack for the app — read prerequisites + acceptance criteria, compare with what you just built
6. Now Support KB: search the two errors you actually hit
7. Community: only for gaps the official sources left open
8. Teach-back: 5 sentences + one diagram from memory, then correct against the docs
